items.name: Readability
items.evidence: This is a one-line change with a short comment, '# Ensure base table is in aliases.', and it is written in the style of the surrounding code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It reuses the existing helper query.get_initial_alias() inside single_alias, adds no copied logic and leaves no dead code. Collector and QuerySet.delete are not touched.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The change is minimal: an idempotent call to get_initial_alias(), with no new error paths and no magic constants. All hidden tests pass (F2P 1/1, P2P 52/52).

items.name: Subquery dropped only for genuine single-table deletes
items.name_zh: 仅在真正单表删除时去掉子查询
items.evidence: The root cause is fixed in single_alias, the same way as the reference. Deletes that join other tables still count more than one alias, so they still use the subquery. The MySQL compiler, which also relies on single_alias, keeps working, and nothing backend-specific was added.
